newsitem.title: INDIA: New SEBI guidelines fail to boost Delhi shares.
newsitem.headline: New SEBI guidelines fail to boost Delhi shares.

text.p: New guidelines announced by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to curb short-selling failed to boost Delhi stocks on Tuesday as shares shed early gains to close lower on profit taking, brokers said.
The Delhi sensitive benchmark index closed 4.25 points down at 700.57.
India's market regulator, SEBI on Monday announced steps to efficiently regulate and increase liquidity in the stock markets.
SEBI chairman D.R. Mehta told reporters after a board meeting in the Indian capital that it would ask short sellers to report their short sales position at the end of each day.

"Despite late selling in shares, I expect market should stage a comeback as bear operators may rush to cover their short positions in line with SEBI's fresh guidelines on short selling," said Vivek Awasthi of brokers Multiple Investments.
Reliance Industries fell 1.50 rupees to 190.35 while TISCO dropped 2.65 rupees to 168.35.
State Bank of India closed 1.60 rupees down at 227.05 and Larsen and Toubro ended 1.20 rupees lower at 232.75.
TELCO lost six rupees at 403 while ITC gained 0.80 rupee at 284.75.
